extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students in complex analysis / Fourier analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and results relating decay/support properties of Fourier transforms to holomorphic extensions and growth of entire functions (Paley–Wiener, Phragmén–Lindelöf, Jensen, Weierstrass products). Includes theorem statements, proofs, examples and exercises used in graduate-level Fourier/complex analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourier inversion validity conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fourier inversion formula f(x) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f(ξ)e^{2π i x ξ} dξ holds under the conditions |f(x)| ≤ A/(1 + x^2) and | f(ξ)| ≤ A/(1 + ξ^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These decay conditions ensure absolute convergence of the inversion integral; reference given to Book I Chapter 5 for a proof. Used as baseline hypotheses for subsequent analytic-extension arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.1 (Exponential decay of transform ⇒ holomorphic strip)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f satisfies | f(ξ)| ≤ A e^{-2π a |ξ|} for some a, A > 0, then f(x) is the restriction to R of a function f(z) holomorphic in the strip S_b = {z ∈ C : |Im(z)| < b} for any 0 < b < a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs entire approximants f_n(z)=∫_{-n}^{n} f(ξ)e^{2π i ξ z} dξ and uses dominated convergence: the integral defining f(z) converges absolutely when b<a because majorant ∫ A e^{-2π a |ξ|} e^{2π b |ξ|} dξ is finite. This is a partial converse to the Paley–Wiener phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.2 (Exponential decay + vanishing on interval ⇒ zero)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(ξ)=O(e^{-2π a |ξ|}) for some a>0, and f vanishes in a non-empty open interval, then f ≡ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because f extends analytically to a strip containing R (by Theorem 3.1), the identity theorem for holomorphic functions implies f is identically zero. Recovers that f and f cannot both have compact support unless f=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.3 (Paley–Wiener theorem: support ⇔ entire extension with exponential type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f is continuous and of moderate decrease on R. Then f has an extension to the complex plane that is entire with |f(z)| ≤ A e^{2π M |z|} for some A>0 if and only if f is supported in [−M, M].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward direction: finite integration range gives entire g(z)=∫_{-M}^{M}f(ξ)e^{2π i ξ z} dξ and |g(z)| ≤ A e^{2π M |z|}. Converse direction requires extra steps: (i) under stronger decay in x plus growth in y one shows f vanishes outside [−M,M] by contour shifts; (ii) weaken hypotheses stepwise (conditions (6)→(7)→theorem) using auxiliary factors (1 ± i ε z)^{-2} and Phragmén–Lindelöf argument to obtain needed bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (6): strong decay/growth hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is entire and satisfies |f(x+iy)| ≤ A/(1 + x^2) e^{2π M |y|}, then f(ξ)=0 for |ξ|>M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: shift contour by ±y and estimate the integral for f(ξ) to get | f(ξ)| ≤ C e^{-2π y(ξ−M)} for ξ>M, then let y→∞ to force f(ξ)=0. Similar for ξ<−M by shifting upward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (7): relaxed growth hypothesis and approximation trick
rubrics_metrics.description: If only |f(x+iy)| ≤ A e^{2π M |y|} holds (no 1/(1+x^2) decay), introduce auxiliary functions f_ε(z)=f(z)/(1+i ε z)^2 which have the 1/(1+x^2)-type decay and converge back to f as ε→0. Use Step 1 result on f_ε and pass to the limit to conclude f vanishes outside [−M,M].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1/(1+i ε z)^2 factor is ≤1 in appropriate half-planes and tends to 1 as ε→0; combined with moderate decrease on R this yields the desired support conclusion after taking limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.4 (Phragmén–Lindelöf theorem for a sector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be holomorphic in the sector S = {z : −π/4 < arg z < π/4}, continuous on its closure, |F(z)| ≤ 1 on the boundary of S, and suppose |F(z)| ≤ C e^{c |z|} for all z in S. Then |F(z)| ≤ 1 for all z ∈ S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof modifies F by multiplying by e^{-ε z^{3/2}} (principal branch) to obtain a bounded holomorphic function that decays at infinity in the sector; apply maximum modulus to limit function and then let ε→0. Remarks show growth restriction is necessary (counterexample e^{z^2}). Exercises generalize to other sector angles and growth exponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Phragmén–Lindelöf to Paley–Wiener proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotate sector to quadrants and consider F(z)=f(z)e^{2π i M z}; boundedness of F on positive real/imaginary axes plus growth control implies by Phragmén–Lindelöf that |F| ≤ 1 in quadrant, hence |f(z)| ≤ e^{2π M y} in first quadrant; analogous arguments give the needed bound in all quadrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the reduction from the weaker growth hypothesis in the theorem to the stronger form used in contour-shift arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.5 (Support on nonnegative frequencies ⇔ upper half-plane extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f and f have moderate decrease. Then f(ξ)=0 for all ξ<0 if and only if f extends to a continuous and bounded function on the closed upper half-plane {y≥0} which is holomorphic in the interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward direction: invert over [0,∞) to define f(z)=∫_0^{∞}f(ξ)e^{2π i z ξ} dξ and show boundedness/holomorphicity. Converse: use approximations f_{ε,δ}(z)=f(z+iδ)/(1−i ε z)^2 holomorphic in region containing closed upper half-plane, show their transforms vanish for ξ<0 and pass to limits to deduce f(ξ)=0 for ξ<0. Analogy noted with Fourier series vanishing of negative coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jensen's formula (Theorem 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f be holomorphic on an open set containing closure of disc D_R, f(0)≠0, and f has no zeros on the circle C_R. If z_1,...,z_N are zeros of f in the disc (counted with multiplicity), then log|f(0)| = Σ_{k=1}^N log(|z_k|/R) + (1/2π)∫_{0}^{2π} log|f(R e^{iθ})| dθ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to product of zero factors and a zero-free holomorphic function g= e^{h}; for g use mean-value property for harmonic Re(h). The identity links interior zeros to boundary average of log|f| and leads to growth-vs-zero-count relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.2 (Integral form of zero counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: With n(r) the number of zeros of f in D_r, Σ_{k=1}^N log(R/|z_k|) = ∫_0^R n(r) (dr/r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses characteristic functions η_k(r)=1_{r>|z_k|} and summation/integration interchange; used to rewrite Jensen's formula as an integral formula for n(r).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: order of an entire function
rubrics_metrics.description: An entire function f has order ≤ ρ if there exist A,B>0 with |f(z)| ≤ A e^{B |z|^ρ} for all z∈C. The order ρ_f is the infimum of such ρ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: e^{z^2} has order 2. This notion controls zero density and growth; used in subsequent theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.1 (Zero-count and summability for finite order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is entire of order ≤ ρ then (i) n(r) ≤ C r^ρ for large r (zero-count grows at most like r^ρ), and (ii) if z_k are zeros (nonzero), then for every s>ρ the series Σ 1/|z_k|^s converges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Jensen's formula and growth bound; gives examples showing s>ρ is sharp (sin πz has order 1 and zeros 1/|n|^s summable iff s>1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3.1 (Criterion for convergence of infinite products)
rubrics_metrics.description:
If Σ |a_n| < ∞ then the product Π_{n=1}^
fty (1 + a_n) converges. The product converges to 0 iff some factor equals 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: for small |a_n| use log(1+a_n) power series and bound |log(1+z)| ≤ 2|z| for |z|<1/2; then exponential of the convergent sum of logs gives convergence of product. This proposition is used to justify building Weierstrass products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3.2 (Uniform convergence of products of holomorphic functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F_n are holomorphic on Ω and constants c_n satisfy Σ c_n < ∞ and |F_n(z) − 1| ≤ c_n for all z∈Ω, then (i) the product Π F_n(z) converges uniformly on Ω to a holomorphic function F(z); (ii) if no F_n vanishes, then the limit of quotients Π F_n^*(z)/F_n(z) equals F^*(z)/F(z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity follows from uniform bounds on |F_n(z)-1|; part (ii) gives a formula for quotient limits and is used when comparing canonical products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula for sine (Weierstrass product example)
rubrics_metrics.description:
sin πz / π = z ∏_{n=1}^
fty (1 − z^2/n^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Derived from the cotangent partial fraction expansion π cot πz = Σ_{n=-∞}^
fty 1/(z+n); compare structural properties (periodicity, poles) and use Liouville's theorem to show quotient of candidate product and sin πz is constant (evaluated at 0 to be 1). This example motivates canonical Weierstrass products and infinite-product techniques.
